title: Frugality Horizon: tenant-level autotuner for batch/caching defaults and quant profiles
author: Noah Kaplan
description: Summary: Introduces the Frugality Horizon autotuner: a tenant-aware automation pipeline that suggests and safely rolls out batching, prefix/KV cache defaults, and per-tenant quantization profile candidates based on sampled telemetry and synthetic workload simulation. Motivation: customers running diverse workloads need predictable unit economics; current defaults are conservative or too generic. This autotuner couples sampled p95/p99 latency, batch hit-rate, token-cost estimates, and model quality regression heuristics to produce prioritized, safe suggestions that can be dry-run via CLI or applied with staged rollouts. What changed: 1) pkg/econ/autotune: core tuning engine, simulation harness, safety gates (latency delta threshold, quality regression window, rollback hooks). 2) cmd/econctl: new CLI for previewing suggestions, running dry-runs, exporting presets-as-yaml, and applying tenant-level rollouts. 3) telemetry/bridge: mapping layer that synthesizes cost-per-token, batch-hit-rate, prefix-cache-hit metrics into the autotuner input format. 4) charts/helm: new helm values for enabling the autotuner and adjusting rollout concurrency. 5) docs/ops: operational runbook, rollback steps, evaluation checklist. 6) tests: unit and end-to-end synthetic-workload tests and a new perf-smoke that runs in CI. Design notes: - Autotuner runs as a controller that processes daily telemetry windows and generates ranked suggestions. - Suggestions include: batching presets (max_batch/target_latency), cache presets (prefix_ttl, kv_cache_allowlist), and quant profiles (int8/llm8/q4_0 variants with estimated PSNR-like quality delta). - Each suggestion carries an estimated delta in unit-cost and a risk score derived from traffic similarity and prior rollouts. - Safety model: suggestions are only applied automatically if they pass low-risk heuristics; otherwise they land in a reviewer queue in the Console and can be applied via econctl with canary/percentage rollouts and automatic rollback triggers. - Dry-run mode: econctl --dry-run produces a synthetic replay of sampled requests against the candidate profile using the simulator and emits a differential report. Checklist: - [x] Core engine implementation - [x] Telemetry mapping and sampling - [x] Simulation harness with synthetic workloads - [x] CLI and docs - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] CI job for perf-smoke Backwards compatibility: the autotuner only produces suggestions; it does not change tenant settings without explicit apply or approved auto-apply policy. The defaults remain unchanged unless opted-in or rolled-out through the Console/CLI. Migration/operational notes: see docs/ops/frugality-horizon-runbook.md for enabling flags, required telemetry retention (30d), and recommended dry-run cadence.
commits: 6 commits: initial engine skeleton; telemetry bridge mapping and sampling; simulation harness + synthetic workloads; econctl CLI and templates; helm values and docs; unit/e2e tests and CI job added.
discussion: Aisha Patel: Nice approach — can we ensure the safety threshold for p95 delta is configurable per-tenant?
Noah Kaplan: Yes, added tenant-level override in engine config; default is 10% p95 increase cap.
Marco Rivera: Simulator looks expensive; what's the expected cost?
Noah Kaplan: We sample 0.1% of traffic by default and use lightweight emulation with token-level cost model; estimated additional infra ~0.5% of nightly batch CPU/GPU time for medium clusters.
Linus Gao: Add an alert if auto-apply causes repeated rollbacks for a tenant.
Noah Kaplan: Added a cooldown circuit breaker with exponential backoff and audit log entry so support can investigate.
QA (Rita Chen): Found flakiness in perf-smoke on small instances; reduced concurrency in CI job and added retry guard.
Aisha Patel: Approved after tests green and perf-smoke passes.
Marco Rivera: Squash-merged to main; applied helm values to staging for a week of soak.
merge_outcome: squash and merge by Aisha Patel (merge commit included link to Linear ENG-1872). Auto-deployment: helm chart values enabled in staging cluster; production enablement requires Ops runbook sign-off.
release_notes: Added Frugality Horizon autotuner: tenant-aware suggestions for batching, cache defaults, and quant profiles. New econctl CLI for dry-runs and staged rollouts. Safe-by-default with configurable safety gates and rollback behavior. Docs and runbook included.
tests_run: Unit tests, integration e2e, perf-smoke (small synthetic workloads), and a 72-hour staging soak under helm values.
